title: Error Budget Runway Fiscalization and Stakeholder Compact
creator: Amina Patel
description: Define a repeatable methodology to translate SLI/SLO targets and observed error-budget burn into a fiscalized "runway" that product, finance, and platform teams can use to prioritize reliability investments. Deliver a stakeholder compact that codifies rollout thresholds, funding triggers, and rollback policies tied to quantified error-budget tranches.
goals: Create a model that converts historical SLI burn rates into a projected error-budget runway expressed in engineering points and approximate dollars per quarter.
Agree with Finance and Product leads on minimum funded runway thresholds that trigger resource allocation or emergent funding requests.
Publish a stakeholder compact (signed by Platform, Core Infra, Product, and Finance) that specifies automated and manual actions at each tranche (green/amber/red).
Instrument dashboards that show real-time runway and forecasted depletion with simple guardrails for on-call and release engineers.
success_metrics: >90% alignment from Platform/Product/Finance on runway calculation formula by end of cycle
Dashboard coverage for top-5 teams serving critical models with forecasted runway and burn > 72% of requests
Reduce surprise fund requests for emergency reliability work by 60% within the next two quarters
Establish automatic throttles/fallbacks for 3 high-impact routes tied to red-tranche breach
scope_included: Design and validate runway calculation using historical SLI windows (30/90/180d) and Monte Carlo forecasting
Define three error-budget tranches (green/amber/red) with explicit actions and responsible roles
Build dashboard widgets in Console for runway, tranche state, and top contributors to burn
Draft stakeholder compact (PDF & Confluence) and run two alignment workshops with Finance/Product/Platform
out_of_scope: Rewriting serving runtime to change kernel selection — optimizations remain separate tickets
Full company-wide SLA changes — this is a program-level compact for core inference surfaces only
Implementing chargeback billing — we'll provide dollar estimates but not an automated billing integration
assumptions: Reliable historical SLI telemetry exists for the last 180 days for the selected endpoints
Finance can accept a bounded estimate (range) of dollars tied to engineering points for initial compact
Platform team can expose an API to surface real-time burn rate and current tranche flag
milestones: 2026-03-05: Draft runway model v0 and toy dataset simulation (in progress)
2026-03-22: Workshop to align on tranche thresholds and funding triggers
2026-04-08: Dashboard prototype with runway widget exposed in Console (alpha)

2026-06-15: Pilot with two product teams and automated amber notifications
risks: Model variance: forecasts may over/under-estimate short-term bursts leading to false confidence
Stakeholder buy-in: Finance may push back on mapping engineering points to dollars without historical chargebacks
Telemetry gaps: missing or inconsistent SLI tags will reduce fidelity for certain routes
Operational burden: added alerts could create alert fatigue if thresholds are too sensitive
